Historically, peritoneal abscesses have been attributed to various causes, including post-surgical complications, intra-abdominal infections like diverticulitis and appendicitis, and penetrating abdominal trauma.
The diagnostic strategies, too, have seen a shift over the past few decades.
Previously, the diagnosis was primarily clinical, relying heavily on physical examination findings and patient history.
However, with the widespread availability and improved resolution of imaging modalities such as ultrasound, CT, and MRI, the accuracy and speed of diagnosis have substantially improved.
Notably, the role of laparoscopy in both the diagnostic and therapeutic realms has also expanded.
